quizName: DMV Practice Test #7 25 Questions • Passing Score 20

questions.question: Who must wear a helmet on a moving motorcycle?
questions.correctAnswerText: All riders and passengers
questions.explanation: All motorcycle riders and passengers must wear a helmet. This includes riders of motorcycles, motor-driven cycles, and motorized bicycles.

questions.question: When another vehicle passes you on the left, what should you do?

options.text: Ride on the right side of your lane.
Ride in the center of your lane.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in the center of your lane.
questions.explanation: When being passed on your left, stay in the center of your lane. Riding on the right side is dangerous because it may encourage the other driver to move back into your lane too soon.

questions.question: What usually causes a "wobble" (sudden shaking of the front wheel and handlebars)?

options.text: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution
Loose connection of the front wheel to the frame
Hitting an object with the front tire

questions.correctAnswerText: Wrong tire pressure or uneven weight distribution
questions.explanation: A wobble is shaking of the front wheel and handlebars. Most wobbles come from improper weight distribution, wrong accessories, or incorrect tire pressure.

questions.question: What does an integrated braking system do?

options.text: It connects the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is used
It automatically brakes based on your riding habits
It applies the brake when you downshift gears

questions.correctAnswerText: It connects the front and rear brakes together when the rear brake is used
questions.explanation: Some motorcycles have integrated braking systems that link the front and rear brakes together when you use the rear brake pedal. Check your owner's manual to understand your motorcycle's braking system.

questions.question: When reacting to a hazard in the road, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Fail to communicate with other drivers
Use your horn, lights, or signals to alert others

questions.correctAnswerText: Fail to communicate with other drivers
questions.explanation: To handle a hazard safely, tell other drivers you are there by using your horn, lights, and signals. Change your speed to fit the situation and adjust your lane position or direction as needed.

questions.question: How fast does the human body remove alcohol?
questions.correctAnswerText: About one drink per hour
questions.explanation: Most people's bodies can remove about one drink per hour. This rate varies from person to person. The safest choice is not to ride after drinking any alcohol.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: No U-turn
questions.explanation: This is a traffic sign with white background and red and black markings. It tells drivers about traffic laws in that area. This sign means U-turns are not allowed.

questions.question: Where are you most likely to have a collision?
questions.correctAnswerText: At an intersection
questions.explanation: Intersections have the most potential for conflicts between you and other traffic.

questions.question: When riding in a group, when should you NOT use a staggered formation?

options.text: When entering or leaving a highway

questions.correctAnswerText: When entering or leaving a highway
questions.explanation: A staggered formation is generally good, but switch to single-file when riding in curves, turning, or entering or leaving a highway.

questions.question: Which statement about motorcycle brakes is true?

options.text: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake
The rear brake is more powerful than the front brake

questions.correctAnswerText: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake
questions.explanation: The front brake is more powerful than the rear brake. It provides at least 70 percent of your motorcycle's total stopping power.

questions.question: How should you brake?
questions.correctAnswerText: With both brakes
questions.explanation: Always use both brakes when you slow down or stop.

questions.question: What does a solid yellow traffic light mean?

options.text: The traffic light is about to change to red.
The traffic light is about to change to green.
Stop and wait for traffic to pass.

questions.correctAnswerText: The traffic light is about to change to red.
questions.explanation: A solid yellow light warns you that the light will change to red soon. Slow down and stop before the intersection if you can do so safely. If you are already in the intersection when the light turns yellow, continue through it.

questions.question: To be effective, eye or face shield protection must:

options.text: Restrict your vision to the sides so you can focus on the road ahead.
Not allow eyeglasses or sunglasses to be worn.

questions.correctAnswerText: Fasten securely.
questions.explanation: A good eye or face shield must fasten securely, be free of scratches, resist damage, allow clear side vision, prevent fogging, and fit over eyeglasses or sunglasses if needed.

questions.question: When traveling at night, you should:

options.text: Ride as fast as you would if riding during the day.
Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
Ride faster than you would if riding during the day.

questions.correctAnswerText: Ride more slowly than you would if riding during the day.
questions.explanation: Ride more slowly at night, especially on roads you do not know well. Slower speeds give you more time to avoid hazards when you cannot see as well.

questions.question: Which lane position is usually best for minimizing the risk of other vehicles sharing your lane?

options.text: The left portion of the lane
The center portion of the lane
The right portion of the lane

questions.correctAnswerText: The center portion of the lane
questions.explanation: Riding in the center of your lane discourages other drivers from squeezing into your space. When you ride behind another vehicle, the center position makes you most visible in their rearview mirror.

questions.question: When entering a turn, it is best to:

options.text: Take the motorcycle out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: Change gears before the turn.
questions.explanation: Change gears before you enter a turn. If you must change gears while turning, do so smoothly.

questions.question: You have an improved chance of avoiding serious injury in a crash if you wear all of the following, except:
questions.correctAnswerText: A sweatshirt.
questions.explanation: A DOT-approved helmet protects your head and neck in a crash. A leather or sturdy synthetic jacket also protects against injury. A sweatshirt does not provide adequate protection.

questions.question: Convex mirrors:

options.text: Provide a narrow view of the road behind you.
Provide a wide view of the road behind you.

questions.correctAnswerText: Provide a wide view of the road behind you.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors show a wider view of the road behind you compared to flat mirrors. They also make objects appear farther away than they really are. Take time to get used to convex mirrors if your motorcycle has them.

questions.question: When riding near a truck:

options.text: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
You should not be able to see the truck's mirrors.
You should concentrate on operating your motorcycle and not worry about the truck's mirrors.

questions.correctAnswerText: If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you.
questions.explanation: Avoid staying in a truck's blind spots. If you cannot see the truck's mirrors, the driver cannot see you either.

questions.question: If a motorcycle is towing a trailer, the motorcyclist's following distance should:

options.text: Be the same as it normally would be.

questions.correctAnswerText: Increase.
questions.explanation: Increase your following distance when towing a trailer. The extra weight means your motorcycle needs more time to stop.

questions.question: When riding in a group on a straight road, how should motorcyclists ride?
questions.correctAnswerText: Ride in a staggered pattern.
questions.explanation: A staggered pattern keeps the group close together while giving each rider enough space. When turning, going around curves, or entering or leaving the road, riders should switch to a single-file line.

questions.question: In dangerous areas, what should a motorcyclist do?

options.text: Hold the clutch and brake levers ready to react quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Hold the clutch and brake levers ready to react quickly.
questions.explanation: In risky areas like intersections, shopping areas, schools, or construction zones, slow down. Hold the clutch and both brake levers ready so you can stop quickly if needed.

questions.question: What does a solid red arrow in a traffic signal mean?
questions.correctAnswerText: Stop completely.
questions.explanation: A solid red arrow means the same as a red light. You must stop and wait for a signal that lets you turn in that direction.

questions.question: If a motorcyclist cannot avoid an obstacle on the road, what should they do?

options.text: Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible.

questions.correctAnswerText: Approach it at a 90-degree angle if possible.
questions.explanation: If you must ride over an obstacle, slow down and hit it at close to a 90-degree angle.

questions.question: Which item is NOT part of a pre-ride inspection?
questions.correctAnswerText: Inspecting paint.
questions.explanation: Before riding, check the tires, controls, lights, signals, mirrors, brakes, oil, fluids, frame, and stands. Paint inspection is not part of a pre-ride safety check.
